accepted.s: Harihara I was crowned on which date at the Virupaksha temple?
accepted.x: Harihara I was crowned on 18 April 1336 at the Virupaksha temple.
accepted.tq: Use the exact date as the deciding clue among closely spaced alternatives.
accepted.sec: Founders' background - Harihara and Bukka, earlier service theories (Kakatiya/Kampili/Delhi), dynasty name, founding year  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the background of Harihara and Bukka:
1. They were sons of Sangama.
2. Sangama is associated with Mangalanilaya.
3. The family is placed in the Kuruba clan by some accounts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Harihara and Bukka were sons of Sangama; Sangama came from Mangalanilaya, and some accounts place the family in the Kuruba clan.
accepted.tq: Combine three related identity clues and eliminate options missing one of them.
accepted.sec: Founders' background - Harihara and Bukka, earlier service theories (Kakatiya/Kampili/Delhi), dynasty name, founding year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Kakatiya-service theory regarding Harihara and Bukka holds that they had served under:
accepted.x: The Kakatiya theory states that Harihara and Bukka served Prataparudra of Warangal before being taken to Delhi after 1323.
accepted.tq: Apply the ruler–regional power association without confusing it with the Kampili or Hoysala theories.
accepted.sec: Founders' background - Harihara and Bukka, earlier service theories (Kakatiya/Kampili/Delhi), dynasty name, founding year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Kampili version concerning Harihara and Bukka?
o: They governed Kampili, were captured by Muhammad bin Tughlaq, converted in Delhi and were sent back as Sultanate governors.
They defeated the Kakatiya ruler Prataparudra and remained in Warangal.
They served Veera Ballala III and founded the empire after the fall of the Hoysala kingdom.
They were sent directly from Sringeri to govern Kampili on behalf of Virupaksha.
accepted.x: The Kampili version states that they governed Kampili, were captured by Muhammad bin Tughlaq, converted in Delhi and later returned as Sultanate governors.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the Kampili, Kakatiya and Kannada/Hoysala versions by matching the complete sequence.
accepted.sec: Founders' background - Harihara and Bukka, earlier service theories (Kakatiya/Kampili/Delhi), dynasty name, founding year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the Delhi-service version, Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent Harihara and Bukka to:
accepted.x: The Delhi-service version says that Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent them to crush Deccan rebels, including the forces associated with Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka and Prolaya Vema.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific assignment attached to the Delhi-service theory.
accepted.sec: Founders' background - Harihara and Bukka, earlier service theories (Kakatiya/Kampili/Delhi), dynasty name, founding year  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the theories concerning the origin of the Vijayanagara founders:
1. The Kannada or Hoysala theory associates them with Veera Ballala III.
2. The Andhra theory is associated with scholars such as N. Venkataramanaiah, Sewell and Nilakanta Sastri.
3. Robert Sewell recorded seven local founding traditions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Kannada/Hoysala theory links them with Veera Ballala III, the Andhra theory has the listed scholarly supporters, and Sewell recorded seven local traditions.
accepted.tq: Test several competing origin theories together rather than relying on one familiar association.
accepted.sec: Founders' background - Harihara and Bukka, earlier service theories (Kakatiya/Kampili/Delhi), dynasty name, founding year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who among the following is associated with the Kannada or Hoysala theory of the origin of Harihara and Bukka?
accepted.x: Father Heras, Rice, S. K. Ayyangar, H. Krishna Sastri and P. B. Desai supported the Kannada or Hoysala theory.
accepted.tq: Separate the scholars supporting the Kannada/Hoysala theory from those associated with the Andhra theory.
accepted.sec: Founders' background - Harihara and Bukka, earlier service theories (Kakatiya/Kampili/Delhi), dynasty name, founding year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The first inscription to call Harihara I a king was the:
accepted.x: The Nellore inscription is regarded as the first inscription to call Harihara I a king; it dates his reign to 1336–1355.
accepted.tq: Match the inscription with the precise historical claim associated with it.
accepted.sec: Founders' background - Harihara and Bukka, earlier service theories (Kakatiya/Kampili/Delhi), dynasty name, founding year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the founding location of Vijayanagara?
o: It was founded on the northern bank of the Tungabhadra in 1323.
It was founded on the southern bank of the Godavari in 1346.
It was founded on the northern bank of the Krishna near Warangal.
It was founded on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra in 1336.
accepted.x: The Vijayanagara kingdom was founded in 1336 on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra.
accepted.tq: Use the river-bank and year together to reject reversed-location options.
accepted.sec: Founders' background - Harihara and Bukka, earlier service theories (Kakatiya/Kampili/Delhi), dynasty name, founding year  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the founding legend, after being defeated while suppressing the Deccan rebellion, Harihara and Bukka met Vidyaranya near:
accepted.x: The legend places their meeting with Vidyaranya near Pampa after their defeat in the Deccan campaign.
accepted.tq: Link the event in the legend with its geographical setting.
accepted.sec: Sites associated with the founders → founding legend, capital's river (Hampi, Vijayanagara, Sringeri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Vidyaranya, who is associated with the reconversion of Harihara and Bukka, was the head of the:
accepted.x: Vidyaranya headed the Sringeri Shankara Math and is associated with the brothers' return to Hinduism.
accepted.tq: Match the religious institution with its associated spiritual leader.
accepted.sec: Sites associated with the founders → founding legend, capital's river (Hampi, Vijayanagara, Sringeri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the sequence in the founding legend?
o: Fall of Warangal → conversion in Delhi → dispatch against Deccan rebels → meeting with Vidyaranya → return to Hinduism
Meeting with Vidyaranya → fall of Warangal → conversion in Delhi → foundation of Anegondi
Conversion in Delhi → fall of Warangal → visit to Sringeri → appointment by Prataparudra
Foundation of Anegondi → conversion in Delhi → fall of Warangal → meeting with Vidyaranya
accepted.x: The legend proceeds from the fall of Warangal and conversion in Delhi to the Deccan campaign, meeting Vidyaranya, and return to Hinduism.
accepted.tq: Arrange the narrative by identifying the first event and following the linked sequence.
accepted.sec: Sites associated with the founders → founding legend, capital's river (Hampi, Vijayanagara, Sringeri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Anegondi is significant in the early history of Vijayanagara because it was:
o: The site of the Sringeri Shankara Math
The place where Saluva Narasimha began the first usurpation
The first seat of the kingdom, established in the name of Sri Virupaksha
The final capital of the Aravidu dynasty
accepted.x: Anegondi was the first seat of the kingdom, and it was set up in the name of Sri Virupaksha.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the founders' first seat from later dynastic capitals and religious centres.
accepted.sec: Sites associated with the founders → founding legend, capital's river (Hampi, Vijayanagara, Sringeri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Vijayanagara was built as a Giri Durga on:
accepted.x: Vijayanagara was built on the south bank of the Tungabhadra as a Giri Durga on Ramadurga hill.
accepted.tq: Test the specific hill associated with the fortified capital.
accepted.sec: Sites associated with the founders → founding legend, capital's river (Hampi, Vijayanagara, Sringeri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations regarding Vijayanagara is correct?
o: Seven earthen ramparts and an extent of 14 × 14 miles
Seven stone ramparts and an extent of 14 × 10 miles
Five stone ramparts and an extent of 10 × 7 miles
Nine stone ramparts and an extent of 18 × 10 miles
accepted.x: Vijayanagara had seven stone ramparts and measured approximately 14 × 10 miles.
accepted.tq: Match both quantitative details; a partially correct numerical option is a deliberate trap.
accepted.sec: Sites associated with the founders → founding legend, capital's river (Hampi, Vijayanagara, Sringeri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The construction of Vijayanagara was completed approximately in _____ and the city was entered in _____.
accepted.x: The city was completed by 1343 and entered in 1344.
accepted.tq: Keep completion and entry dates in their correct chronological order.
accepted.sec: Sites associated with the founders → founding legend, capital's river (Hampi, Vijayanagara, Sringeri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The term ‘Hampi’ is associated with which of the following?
o: The capital founded by Tirumala Raya at Penukonda
Pampa region, where the brothers met Vidyaranya
The Kalyani origin of the Saluva dynasty
The place where Vira Narasimha was crowned in 1505
accepted.x: Hampi, or Pampa, was the region where Harihara and Bukka met Vidyaranya according to the founding tradition.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Hampi/Pampa from the later capitals and dynastic centres.
accepted.sec: Sites associated with the founders → founding legend, capital's river (Hampi, Vijayanagara, Sringeri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Harihara and Bukka visited Sringeri in 1346 after:
o: The fall of the Saluva dynasty
accepted.x: The brothers visited Sringeri in 1346 after the Hoysala victory.
accepted.tq: Associate the date with the specific event rather than with the founding year.
accepted.sec: Sites associated with the founders → founding legend, capital's river (Hampi, Vijayanagara, Sringeri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the legend associated with the selection of the capital site, a hare:
o: Turned on the royal hunting dogs
Was offered to the deity Virupaksha
Led the royal hunting party to Sringeri
Crossed the Tungabhadra during a battle
accepted.x: The site was considered a place of valour because a hare reportedly turned on the royal hunting dogs.
accepted.tq: Use the unusual legend detail to distinguish the correct option from plausible religious associations.
accepted.sec: Sites associated with the founders → founding legend, capital's river (Hampi, Vijayanagara, Sringeri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Vijayanagara dynasties in chronological order of their rule:
A. Tuluva
B. Aravidu
C. Sangama
D. Saluva
accepted.x: The dynastic order was Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu.
accepted.tq: Fix the first dynasty and then place the successive dynasties in their established order.
accepted.sec: Dynasties of Vijayanagara in order (Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu) - founders  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Dynasty)
a. Sangama
b. Saluva
c. Tuluva
d. Aravidu

List-II (Founder)
i. Tirumala Raya
ii. Saluva Narasimha
iii. Harihara I and Bukka I
iv. Vira Narasimha

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Sangama was founded by Harihara I and Bukka I, Saluva by Saluva Narasimha, Tuluva by Vira Narasimha, and Aravidu by Tirumala Raya.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure founder–dynasty pair and complete the one-to-one matching.
accepted.sec: Dynasties of Vijayanagara in order (Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu) - founders  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Aravidu followed the Tuluva dynasty and is generally dated from 1570 to about 1680. The other three dynasty spans are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed or misplaced dynastic span rather than the familiar correct pairs.
accepted.sec: Dynasties of Vijayanagara in order (Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu) - founders  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The first usurpation in the history of the Vijayanagara Empire is associated with:
o: Saluva Narasimha and the Saluva dynasty
Harihara I and the Sangama dynasty
Tirumala Raya and the Aravidu dynasty
Vira Narasimha and the Tuluva dynasty
accepted.x: Saluva Narasimha ended the Sangama line and established the Saluva dynasty, an event described as the first usurpation.
accepted.tq: Match the political event ‘first usurpation’ with its ruler and dynasty.
accepted.sec: Dynasties of Vijayanagara in order (Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu) - founders  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Tuluva dynasty is correct?
o: Tirumala Raya founded the Tuluva dynasty at Chandragiri.
Krishnadevaraya founded the Tuluva dynasty in 1570.
Vira Narasimha was crowned in 1505 after executing Immadi Narasimha.
Tuluva Narasa Nayaka was crowned in 1485 after defeating Saluva Narasimha.
accepted.x: The APPSC-associated account identifies Vira Narasimha as the founder; he was crowned in 1505 after executing Immadi Narasimha. Tuluva Narasa Nayaka was his father and is also called the dynasty founder in another historiographical usage.
accepted.tq: Separate the formal APPSC founder attribution from the alternative genealogical description of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka.
accepted.sec: Dynasties of Vijayanagara in order (Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu) - founders  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Aravidu dynasty?
o: Founder—Tirumala Raya; capitals—Penukonda, Chandragiri and Vellore
accepted.x: Tirumala Raya founded the Aravidu dynasty, whose capitals included Penukonda, Chandragiri and Vellore.
accepted.tq: Check both the founder and the capital list before selecting the complete pair.
accepted.sec: Dynasties of Vijayanagara in order (Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu) - founders  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which dynasty of Vijayanagara ruled for the longest period and had Devaraya II as its greatest ruler and Praudha Raya as its last ruler?
accepted.x: The Sangama dynasty was the longest-ruling dynasty; Devaraya II was regarded as its greatest ruler and Praudha Raya as its last ruler.
accepted.tq: Combine the duration, greatest ruler and last ruler to identify the dynasty.
accepted.sec: Dynasties of Vijayanagara in order (Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu) - founders  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the religious affiliation and emblem of the Vijayanagara dynasties:
1. The emblem was the Varaha or boar.
2. The Sangamas were Shaiva.
3. The later three dynasties were Vaishnava.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Vijayanagara emblem was the Varaha. The Sangama rulers were Shaiva, while the Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu dynasties were associated with Vaishnavism.
accepted.tq: Test the common emblem separately from the Shaiva–Vaishnava dynastic distinction.
accepted.sec: Dynasties of Vijayanagara in order (Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu) - founders  [APPSC]
